task: send money to a person on a payment app (Venmo, Zelle, Cash App, PayPal): pick or add the recipient, enter the amount and note, review the recipient and amount at the pre-send screen — the no-undo moment — and send; complete when the sent confirmation / completed payment is on screen. Surface pinned: a payment app or a bank app's send-money screen, mobile or web. Variants: requesting money or splitting a bill (seeded variant), paying a merchant at checkout, and bank-to-bank account transfers do not belong.

questions.question: Did a transient success animation appear before the app returned to the home screen?
questions.why: Some apps, like Cash App, do not leave a static confirmation screen; they show a brief success animation (like a checkmark) and immediately return to the home screen, making it the only immediate proof of success.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to witness the brief visual confirmation of success, forcing them to manually dig through their transaction history to verify the payment went through if the agent misses it.

questions.question: Do the transaction amounts and details across the initial balance, the review screen, and the final confirmation agree with each other?
questions.why: Verifying the recipient, amount, and privacy settings on the review screen against your starting balance ensures the math is correct before you pass the no-undo moment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally audit the transaction across its different stages to ensure your account balance reflects the exact payment made.

questions.question: Where do you navigate to view your payment transaction history?
questions.why: Opening the settings menu from the chats tab is necessary to access your payment logs and verify the transaction.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose direct visibility into your account settings and the peace of mind of independently verifying the payment log yourself.

questions.question: Which transaction's details do you want to view?
questions.why: The screen shows the chats tab with a recent payment snippet of '₹1.00 · Testing', and selecting the correct thread allows you to verify the final transaction details.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally review the final payment record in your chat history to ensure the transaction was completed correctly.

questions.question: Does the transaction appear in your activity feed, and what is its current status?
questions.why: Verifying the transaction in the activity screen confirms the payment was successfully initiated and shows if it is still pending.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the immediate reassurance of seeing the transaction recorded in your own account history and knowing its exact status.

questions.question: No confirmation appeared on screen - does the Activity list actually show the payment as sent?
questions.why: Since the confirmation was not immediately displayed on screen, you must navigate to the Activity tab to verify the transaction.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the direct reassurance of seeing the final transaction record with your own eyes to guarantee the money was sent.

questions.question: Is the payment status completed, and what is the transaction ID to share with the recipient?
questions.why: Verifying the completed status and capturing the transaction ID ensures the payment was successful and provides proof to share with the recipient.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the immediate reassurance of seeing the completed status and the ability to personally copy the transaction ID for the recipient.

questions.question: Did the transaction trigger a security hold that requires your out-of-band approval?
questions.why: Large or unusual peer-to-peer payments often trigger automated bank holds, requiring you to respond to a text or email from your bank before the funds are actually released.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the awareness that the payment is paused and the opportunity to promptly clear the security hold, leaving the recipient waiting for funds you thought were sent.

questions.question: Is the payment status showing as 'Pending Review' rather than completed?
questions.why: Fraud algorithms sometimes hold payments for manual review, meaning the recipient will not get the money instantly as expected.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the awareness that your payment is delayed by the platform, preventing you from communicating the delay to the recipient.

questions.question: Does your final account balance confirm that the payment was actually sent?
questions.why: The account balance remained at $0.00, proving that the $1.00 transaction drafted earlier was never actually submitted.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to verify that the funds actually left your account and the transaction was successfully completed.

questions.question: Has your available balance decreased to reflect the payment, even if the transaction history hasn't updated?
questions.why: Verifying that the available balance dropped from $685.52 to $680.52 confirms the payment was processed, even though the recent transactions list doesn't show it yet.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the immediate reassurance of seeing your account balance decrease to confirm the transfer was successful before the transaction log updates.

questions.question: Do you need to refresh the screen to verify the updated account balance?
questions.why: The screen still displays the previous available balance of $680.52, so refreshing is necessary to confirm the transaction was processed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means losing the immediate reassurance of seeing your funds successfully update in real time.

questions.question: Is the transaction visible in your recent activity and reflected in your updated balance?
questions.why: Verifying the recent transactions list and the available balance ensures the payment was fully processed and recorded.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the peace of mind that comes from personally confirming your funds settled correctly in the account history.

questions.question: What confirmation will I receive after sending the money?
questions.why: Knowing that Zelle sends confirmation emails to both parties provides peace of mind that the transaction completed successfully.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the immediate reassurance of checking your own inbox to verify the transaction went through and the recipient was notified.

questions.question: Which notifications confirm the money transfer was successful?
questions.why: Checking the text message and Gmail notification from Capital One provides immediate proof that the transaction was completed and acknowledged by the recipient.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means missing the personal reassurance of seeing the recipient's direct text message and the official bank confirmation.

questions.question: Is the transfer complete, or does the recipient need to register first?
questions.why: This matters because the confirmation screen warns that the recipient is unregistered and your account will not be debited until they sign up.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the awareness that their payment is currently pending and requires the recipient to take action before the money actually moves.

questions.question: Do you want to verify the instructions the recipient receives to claim the money?
questions.why: The email shows the recipient must click a button to claim the money within 24 hours before the payment expires.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to understand exactly what steps the recipient must take to access the funds.
questions.verify_form: Check whether anyone verified the claim side - the email gives your recipient 24 hours before the payment dies; if the agent skipped that, the send can quietly expire.

questions.question: Is your payment confirmed, and does the recipient need to take action to receive it?
questions.why: This matters because the screen confirms the send but warns that the deposit is pending the recipient's action.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The delegator loses the immediate knowledge that their recipient might need to manually accept the payment to get the funds.

questions.question: Do you need to download a receipt or just verify the final transfer status?
questions.why: The screen shows the transfer is currently 'In review' and provides the final exchange rate along with options to download a statement or report an issue.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally verify the estimated delivery timeline and decide if you need to keep a downloaded record of the transaction.
questions.verify_form: Check whether a receipt got saved - the screen offered a download and the agent chose; with no file kept, this transfer's proof lives only inside the app.

questions.question: Do you want to save or print a PDF copy of this receipt?
questions.why: The screen displays a browser print dialog with a preview of the transaction details, offering the option to save a permanent record of the completed payment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to decide whether to keep a personal, offline record of the transaction receipt for your own files.
questions.verify_form: The print dialog was open and got cancelled - check whether you wanted a PDF or paper copy; the transaction ID on it is what you would quote in a dispute.

children.label: Receive or withdraw the money
children.note: 9.1 when money comes in; 9.2 then 9.3 then 9.4 to move a balance out to a bank

questions.question: What are the details of the transaction you just received?
questions.why: The screen displays the sender, amount, and completed status, confirming the exact details of the transfer.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the immediate reassurance of personally verifying the completed transaction details and knowing the money was successfully processed.

questions.question: Did the payment successfully post to your Apple Pay Cash balance?
questions.why: Checking the last transaction on the Apple Pay Cash card confirms that the money was actually received and added to the balance.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the peace of mind that comes from independently verifying the completed transaction in your own Wallet app history.

questions.question: Do the sender names on the sending and receiving receipts match?
questions.why: The receipt on the receiving device lists the sender as "[name]", but the sending device lists "[name]", revealing a discrepancy in the transaction records.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to realize that the payment was processed under an unexpected or mismatched account name.

questions.question: Should you transfer your current balance to a bank account?
questions.why: The screen displays a $10 Apple Pay Cash balance and requires adding a full bank account number to initiate a transfer.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the privacy of keeping their full bank account number secure and the choice of which specific bank receives the funds.
questions.verify_form: Check whether a transfer to the bank was started and for how much - moving your balance out is a withdrawal you may never have asked for.

questions.question: How do you proceed when your available balance is zero and the next button is inactive?
questions.why: The screen displays a $0.00 Venmo balance, which disables the Next button and prevents the transfer from being executed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the immediate feedback that the account lacks funds and the choice to verbally explain the steps rather than attempting an impossible action.

children.label: Choose the transfer speed and fee

questions.question: Should you pay a fee for an instant transfer to your bank, or wait up to three days for a free transfer?
questions.why: The screen presents a choice between paying for an instant transfer or waiting up to three business days for a free transfer to your linked bank account.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether the speed of an instant transfer is worth the associated fee based on your current financial urgency.
questions.verify_form: The agent picked a transfer speed - check whether it took the instant option and its fee or the free three-day one; paying for speed you didn't ask for is a preference, not a default.

children.label: Set the transfer amount and destination

questions.question: How much of your cash balance do you want to transfer, and to which linked bank account?
questions.why: The screen displays your current Apple Pay Cash balance and the destination bank account, requiring you to specify the exact amount to move.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose control over your immediate liquidity, as an agent might transfer funds you intended to keep in the app or send them to the wrong linked account.
questions.verify_form: The agent set the withdrawal - check the amount and destination account on the transfer screen; moving the full balance somewhere you didn't name is exactly the mistake this screen invites.

questions.question: Did the bank transfer ever resolve? The confirmation warns it takes 1 to 3 business days, and nothing afterward shows it completing.
questions.why: The confirmation screen states that transfers take 1 to 3 business days, so the video concludes before the payment fully clears.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the certainty of knowing the transfer successfully cleared the bank after the pending period.
